title: The row menu and Skip; a skipped row returns on its own
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in as a service advisor with view customers (and edit customers to add or change a record), on the build under test. The Maintenance Reminders feature is on (behind the maintenance_reminders flag).
  2. Open an asset page and its Maintenance tab (the last tab, after Notes). The asset card is on the left; the Compliance section sits below Contact.
  3. An enrolled unit on its Maintenance tab. Seed it: enrol an asset (asset Maintenance tab -> Enrol -> pick a schedule).
  4. The unit has a routine service row and a compliance service row that are due.
custom_steps:
1. Open a routine row's menu, then a compliance row's menu, and read the actions.
  2. Skip a routine service and check the asset row and the worklist.
  3. Give the unit a new reading (or work order) and check the routine row returns; change a compliance record and check its row returns.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • A routine service row offers Mark complete, Create work order, Skip and Other triggers; a compliance service row offers Mark complete, Create work order and Skip.
  • Skip hides the row from the worklist; on the asset tab the row stays with a grey "Skipped" badge and its date unchanged, its menu offers Undo skip (and for compliance "+ Add record"), and Skip moves no date and records no completion.
  • A skipped routine service returns to the worklist on a new reading or work order; a skipped compliance service returns when its record changes.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-3780; story SV-10566 (S9, The asset Maintenance tab); Chunk 1 MR spec (Confluence 886931488), S9 (confidence display copied from S11); read 29 Sep 2026. Source-verified 29 September 2026; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S9-R9: “A routine service row offers Mark complete, Create work order, Skip, and Other triggers”
  • S9-R11: “A compliance service row offers Mark complete, Create work order and Skip”
  • S9-R13: “Skip means the shop knows the service is due and is not acting on it now. It hides the row from the worklist; on the asset tab the row stays with a grey Skipped badge and its date unchanged ... Skip moves no date and records no completion”
  • S9-R18: “A skipped routine service comes back on the worklist when the asset gets a new reading or a new work order. A skipped compliance service comes back when its record changes”
  • S9-E4: “A unit off the road, or a customer having the inspection done elsewhere, is what Skip is for”
